ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.AnyEnemy)` (Pillage.cs:17-20) == cost 1 / ATTACK / UNCOMMON / ANY_ENEMY.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DamageVar(6m, ValueProp.Move)` (Pillage.cs:15) == `_damage = 6`, powered on both sides. The draw count is unbounded and so has no var on either side.

OnPlay.rationale: Attack first, then C#'s do/while: `do { cardModel = await CardPileCmd.Draw(choiceContext, Owner); } while (cardModel != null && cardModel.Type == CardType.Attack && CardPile.GetCards(Owner, PileType.Hand).Count() < CardPile.MaxCardsInHand)` (Pillage.cs:29-33). All three termination conditions are reproduced, and the DO-WHILE shape matters -- at least one card is always drawn, even if the hand is already at 9 and the first draw fills it. The sim's loop draws first (pillage.py:84), then breaks if nothing came (85-86, standing in for C#'s `cardModel != null` when the piles are empty), then if the drawn card is not an Attack (87-88), then if the hand is now full (89-90) -- the same order as C#'s three `while` clauses. MaxCardsInHand is 10 on both sides (CardPile.cs:21, player.py:56).

guards.what: the sim identifies the drawn card as `player.hand[-1]` (pillage.py:87) where C# uses the value the single-card Draw overload returns
guards.issue: C#'s single-card `CardPileCmd.Draw` overload RETURNS the card it drew (Pillage.cs:30) and the type test reads that value; the sim infers the drawn card from list order as `player.hand[-1]` (pillage.py:87). Equivalent only while draws append to the end of the hand and nothing inserts after them. A draw-time hook that put a card into the hand at any position other than the end -- or after the drawn one -- would make the sim test the WRONG CARD's type and so terminate or continue the do/while loop wrongly, changing both the cards drawn and the draw count. DORMANT: no ported hook inserts into the hand during a draw (the ported draw hooks add to the DRAW pile or exhaust, not to a hand position). TRIGGER: any ported `on_card_drawn` / draw-time listener that adds a card to the hand, or any hand insert at a position other than the end -- `CardPilePosition` is already a modelled concept for the draw pile (see card/metamorphosis). Recorded as a gap rather than faithful because the sim reads a different thing than the source does; the outcomes coincide today, which is dormancy, not equivalence.
